title: PhysiCalWorld: In-Context Physics Calibration for World Models
why_read: An interesting approach to making world models adapt to unknown physical properties like friction or mass on the fly, relevant to robotics and simulation researchers.
analysis: World models predict how a scene will change given actions, but they often ignore hidden physical properties like friction or joint damping that aren't visible in a single frame, causing prediction drift in new scenes. PhysiCalWorld addresses this by encoding a short exploratory interaction into a compact 'physics descriptor' that conditions later predictions, without needing explicit physics equations or fine-tuning. This descriptor is computed once and reused cheaply across many rollouts, which is a practical efficiency touch. The idea of in-context physics calibration is a useful contribution for robotics planning and simulation-based control.
